paragraphs: Avtulmos. Eruvin, chapter 3, mishnah 4, 35a: Rabbi Yose said that Avtulmos testified in the name of five elders that a doubtful eruv is valid. Rosh Hashanah, first chapter, 15a, and Sukkah 40a: Rabbi Yose said Avtulmos testified in the name of five elders that an etrog follows its picking for tithing. At the end of Sotah, 49, and end of chapter Merubbeh, 83a: Avtulas ben Reuven was permitted to cut his hair komei because he was close to the government. I saw in Me'ilah that Reuven the Itztrobuli was permitted to cut his hair, etc.; perhaps he was his father (see there). In Me'ilah, before Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yose came to Rome, he nullified the decree and was close to the government. Apparently, they did not recognize him as a Jew [the digital witness reads ולא הכיתי, literally “and I did not strike”; conjectural repair]. When they recognized him, the decree was restored, until Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai came and nullified it. In a baraita his son is a tanna, Rabbi Yonatan; he was Rabbi Yose’s teacher. Some versions read Avshulim or Avtulas; another reading: ben Avtulmos (Mekhilta, Mishpatim, section 3: ben Avtulmas). Rabbi Natan ben Avtulmas; Rabbi Shimon ben Avtulmos.
